_meta.verified_against: Appendix A Requirements Compliance Matrix pp.102-117 + overview table pp.11-12
notes: FC classification begins at FCR 10, not FCR 9.
FCR 9 is NFC composite/bonded additional activities — it is NOT an FC requirement.
FCR 21 and FCR 22 apply to FC parts AND NFC composite/bonded parts only, NOT all NFC parts.
KIc/Fty >= 0.33 sqrt(in) is a criterion under FCR 8 section 6.2.5.a(2) for metallic NFC low-risk classification. It does NOT belong to FCR 22.

fcrs.title: Fracture Control Plan (FCP)
fcrs.description: A Fracture Control Plan shall be developed and maintained by the program for human-rated spaceflight hardware.
fcrs.notes: Overarching requirement. FCP documents classification approaches, RFCB review, and all downstream activities.

fcrs.title: NASA Implementation
fcrs.description: Requires implementation of fracture control by NASA.
fcrs.notes: Organizational requirement. MIRA does not implement this — it informs users that it exists.

fcrs.title: Program Implementation
fcrs.description: Requires implementation of fracture control by the program.
fcrs.notes: Organizational requirement.

fcrs.title: RFCB Involvement
fcrs.description: Requires Responsible Fracture Control Board (RFCB) involvement in fracture control activities.
fcrs.notes: MIRA outputs reference the RFCB wherever approval or review is required. RFCB is NOT an automated gate — it is a human process.

fcrs.title: Evaluate All Parts for Classification
fcrs.description: All parts used in human-rated spaceflight hardware shall be evaluated for fracture control classification.
fcrs.notes: This is the entry point for MIRA classification wizard. Every part gets evaluated — none are skipped.

fcrs.title: Exempt Classification Criteria
fcrs.description: Each part classified as exempt shall fit into one of the following: (a) non-structural parts with no credible failure mode caused by a flaw; (b) non-structural parts with no credible potential for causing a catastrophic hazard; (c) other non-structural parts approved by the RFCB for exempt status.
fcrs.notes: EXEMPT parts are non-structural. No further fracture control activity required. Category (c) requires RFCB approval — MIRA flags this. Do NOT conflate EXEMPT with NFC documented non-hazardous failure mode (FCR 8 §6.2.6) — that category can include structural parts with documented hazard assessments.

fcrs.title: NFC Established Approaches — Specific Hardware Types
fcrs.description: To be classified as NFC, each part described by a specific hardware type shall comply with the established approach for that type: (a) metallic fasteners, rivets, shear pins, locking devices; (b) shatterable components and structures; (c) rotating hardware; (d) sealed containers; (e) tools, mechanisms, tethers; (f) batteries.

subtypes.description: NFC metallic fasteners, rivets, shear pins, locking devices
NFC batteries (except button cells <=200 mA-hr and small carbon-zinc/zinc-air)

fcrs.notes: Composite and bonded hardware in these categories must ALSO satisfy FCR 9 (section 6.3).

fcrs.title: NFC General Approaches
fcrs.description: Each part classified as NFC that is not a specific hardware type per section 6.1 shall comply with one of: (a) NFC low-released mass; (b) NFC contained; (c) NFC fail-safe; (d) NFC NHLBB pressurized; (e) NFC low-risk; (f) NFC documented non-hazardous failure mode.

criteria: Well-characterized strength and ductility, processes established to be extremely unlikely to produce flawed parts, no brittle fracture
KIc/Fty >= 1.66 sqrt(mm) [0.33 sqrt(in)] AND no sensitivity to EAC, SLC, or SCC per NASA-STD-6016
Al parts: not loaded short-transverse if dimension > 7.62 cm (3 in)
Net-section stresses at limit load < 30% of ultimate strength
One of: (A) fatigue analysis >= 4 service lives with 1.5x on cyclic stress, OR (B) damage tolerance analysis >= 4 service lives with 1.5x on alternating stress using 0.127 mm (0.005 in) initial crack
metallic_criteria.note: KIc/Fty >= 0.33 sqrt(in) is ONE of FIVE criteria for NFC low-risk metallic. Meeting this ratio alone does NOT classify the part as NFC low-risk. Additively manufactured parts do NOT qualify as low-risk per NASA-STD-6030 AMR15.

criteria: Residual strength with largest RTD flaw sustains DUL (analysis + coupon/element test data)
Limit strain with RTD flaw size below no-growth threshold strain (established by test)
Reflight: visual inspection confirms hardware intact before reuse

subtypes.description: NFC documented non-hazardous failure mode — documented hazard assessment shows no credible catastrophic hazards from flaw-caused failure

fcrs.notes: Composite and bonded hardware in all 8a-8f subcategories must ALSO satisfy FCR 9 (section 6.3). Metallic welds and castings do not qualify as low-risk (8e) unless inspection data confirms no flaws can grow.

fcrs.title: Additional Activities for Composite/Bonded NFC Hardware
fcrs.description: NFC composite or bonded parts that satisfy a category in sections 6.1 or 6.2 shall ALSO comply with: (a) for NFC low-risk: DTA per 7.4.1, IDMP per 7.4.2, RTD per 7.4.3; (b) for other NFC: flaw definition and quantification, IDMP per 7.4.2; (c) NDE after all manufacturing processes (with exceptions for low-released mass and contained); (d) FCR 21 traceability; (e) FCR 22 materials requirements.
fcrs.notes: FCR 9 is NFC — NOT fracture-critical. It is an additional overlay requirement for composite/bonded parts regardless of their NFC subcategory. FCR 21 and FCR 22 are triggered by FCR 9 for NFC composite/bonded parts.

fcrs.title: Fracture-Critical (FC) Classification Criteria
fcrs.description: Parts shall be classified as fracture critical UNLESS: (a) there is no credible possibility for a flaw in the part to cause failure during the part lifetime, OR (b) part failure does not result in a credible catastrophic hazard. Default is fracture-critical if in doubt.
fcrs.notes: FC is the default classification when EXEMPT and NFC cannot be demonstrated. When load_path_type or hazard_consequence is unknown, classify as FC (indeterminate -> conservative fallback = FC). FC parts commonly include: rotating hardware not meeting 6.1.3, hazardous fluid containers, pressurized structures, primary thrust structure, solid rocket motor cases/nozzles, habitable modules. Pressure vessels are always FC.

fcrs.title: FC Established Approaches — Specific Hardware Types
fcrs.description: Each FC part described by a specific hardware type shall comply with the established approach: (a) FC metallic pressure vessels; (b) FC composite overwrapped pressure vessels (COPVs); (c) FC pressurized structures; (d) FC unpressurized primary structure; (e) FC rotating hardware; (f) FC fluid conductors and fittings; (g) FC solid rocket motor cases and nozzles; (h) FC battery cases; (i) FC shatterable components and structures; (j) FC tools, mechanisms, and tethers.

subtypes.description: FC solid rocket motor cases and nozzles

fcrs.notes: Phase 1: identify which subtype applies and route to appropriate assessment path. FCR 12 applies when the part is metallic FC but NOT covered by 7.2 subtypes or 7.5.

fcrs.title: General Approach — Metallic FC Parts
fcrs.description: General approach for fracture critical metallic parts assessment not covered by FCR 11 (section 7.2) or FCR 14 (section 7.5).
fcrs.notes: This is the fallback for FC metallic hardware that doesn't match a specific FCR 11 subtype. Requires damage tolerance analysis (DTA) including: initial flaw assumption per FCR 15, fracture mechanics analysis per 7.3.2, fatigue crack growth, critical flaw size at fracture.

fcrs.title: General Approach — Composite/Bonded FC Parts
fcrs.description: General approach for fracture critical composite or bonded hardware assessment not covered by FCR 11 (section 7.2) or FCR 14 (section 7.5).
fcrs.notes: Requires DTA per 7.4.1, IDMP per 7.4.2, RTD per 7.4.3. More complex than metallic path because composite properties are often unique to the fabricated assembly.

fcrs.title: Optional FC Approaches
fcrs.description: Optional approaches and activities for specific FC hardware types not covered in section 7.2.
fcrs.notes: Phase 2 consideration. Includes special cases like fracture critical hardware with unique assessment approaches approved by RFCB.

fcrs.title: Flaw Screen Requirement
fcrs.description: Fracture critical parts (and NFC composite/bonded per FCR 9) shall be screened for flaws using NDE or proof testing. Standard flaw sizes from NASA-STD-5009C Tables 1 and 2: surface crack 0.050 in (1.27 mm) depth, embedded crack 0.100 in (2.54 mm) depth for Standard NDE methods.
fcrs.notes: Standard NDE flaw sizes are in NASA-STD-5009C Table 1 (metric) and Table 2 (inches). These are initial crack sizes for DTA. 90/95 POD (90% probability of detection at 95% confidence) required. Source for initial_flaw_sizes.json.

fcrs.title: NDE for Metallic FC Parts
fcrs.description: NDE requirements for fracture critical metallic parts per NASA-STD-5009C.
fcrs.notes: References NASA-STD-5009C directly. NDE must meet Standard NDE requirements unless Special or Custom NDE is approved by RFCB.

fcrs.title: NDE for Composite/Bonded FC Parts
fcrs.description: NDE requirements for fracture critical composite or bonded parts. Also applies to NFC composite/bonded per FCR 9.
fcrs.notes: NDE performed after all manufacturing processes (or after proof test if proof test is used). No NDE required for NFC low-released mass or NFC contained composite/bonded parts.

fcrs.title: Optional Proof Test
fcrs.description: If proof testing is used as the flaw screening technique for fracture critical parts, the approach shall be documented in the FCP with rationale approved by the RFCB.
fcrs.notes: Optional path. Phase 2 consideration.

fcrs.title: Optional Process Controls
fcrs.description: If process controls are used to establish bounds on flaw sizes in fracture critical parts, approach must be documented in FCP, rationale documented, FCP approved by RFCB.
fcrs.notes: Optional path. Phase 2 consideration.

fcrs.title: Detected Flaw Assessment
fcrs.description: Spaceflight hardware with detected flaws used for flight without repair or replacement shall have a specific detailed assessment approach documented in the FCP. For metallic: upper bound flaw size, upper bound crack growth rate, lower bound critical stress intensity, lower bound fatigue crack growth threshold (Kth). For composite/bonded: approach and rationale to RFCB for approval.
fcrs.notes: Phase 2 consideration. MIRA Phase 1 flags that detected flaws require documented assessment — does not perform the assessment itself.

fcrs.title: Traceability for FC and NFC Composite/Bonded Parts
fcrs.description: Traceability for each fracture critical and NFC composite or bonded part shall be established and maintained by providing a unique serial number (or other method) and a complete life history including: load history, impact damage, repair, materials, manufacturing, processing, and environmental exposure.
fcrs.notes: Applies to FC parts AND NFC composite/bonded parts. Does NOT apply to NFC metallic parts. MIRA outputs this as a required action when classification is FC or NFC_COMPOSITE_BONDED.

fcrs.title: Materials Selection and Usage for FC and NFC Composite/Bonded Parts
fcrs.description: The selection, processing, and use of materials for all fracture critical and NFC composite or bonded parts shall include ALL of the following, documented in the FCSR: (a) supplier data certifications; (b) materials compatible with NASA-approved Standards and Specifications; (c) account for operating conditions on damage tolerance properties (temperature, environment, coatings, proof test fluids, loading spectra, etc.); (d) design and assess with representative test data (material processed to same thickness, condition, and orientation in worst-case combination, OR fully traceable material condition throughout fabrication and service); (e) derived strength and damage tolerance data from NASA-approved sources, conservatively bounded if lacking, determined by testing if needed, approved by RFCB; (f) approved MUA for any materials not qualified per NASA-STD-6016; (g) all MUAs documented in FCSR.
full_requirements: a. Fabricate from materials with supplier data certifications
b. Materials compatible with NASA-approved Standards and Specifications
c. Account for operating condition effects on damage tolerance properties
d. Design and assess with representative test data (worst-case thickness/condition/orientation, or fully traceable)
e. Derived data from NASA-approved sources; conservatively bounded or tested if lacking; RFCB approval for testing
f. Approved MUA for any materials not qualified per NASA-STD-6016
g. All MUAs documented in FCSR
fcrs.notes: Applies to FC parts AND NFC composite/bonded parts. Does NOT apply to NFC metallic-only parts. CRITICAL: KIc/Fty >= 0.33 sqrt(in) is NOT an FCR 22 requirement — it is FCR 8 section 6.2.5.a(2) for NFC low-risk metallic classification. Phase 1 MIRA materials_checker.py supports FCR 22 by checking: supplier certs (flagged as required), NASA-approved spec compatibility (MMPDS v1), and MUA flags for non-standard materials. Items (c), (d), (e) require RFCB-approved DTA — Phase 2 scope.

fcrs.title: Engineering Drawing Identification for FC Parts
fcrs.description: Fracture critical parts shall be identified on engineering drawings in the notes of the individual part drawing, along with inspections, serialization, and other pertinent information necessary to maintain traceability.
fcrs.notes: MIRA outputs this as a required action for FC classification. The actual drawing update is a human/engineering task — MIRA does not modify drawings.

fcrs.title: Fracture Control Summary Report (FCSR)
fcrs.description: An FCSR shall be developed by the spaceflight hardware program/project that: (a) documents the basis for acceptance that all flight hardware parts have met fracture control requirements in the approved FCP; (b) contains detailed information or reference to detailed information for all parts including evaluations, classification, assessments, inspections, and disposition; (c) documents all analyses and tests on representative flight hardware used for certification.
fcrs.notes: MIRA classification output feeds into the FCSR — it does not generate the FCSR. Phase 1 outputs flag that an FCSR is required and list what must be documented in it.

fcrs.title: Verification Requirement
fcrs.description: Verification that fracture control requirements have been met shall be performed and documented.
fcrs.notes: Organizational verification requirement. MIRA outputs flag verification as a required step — does not perform verification.

fcrs.title: Alternative Approaches
fcrs.description: Alternatives to prescribed approaches in sections 5, 6, 7, or 8 may be proposed. Alternative approaches must be accompanied by supporting rationale establishing comparable rigor, presented to RFCB for review and approval, and documented in the specialized FCP.
fcrs.notes: MIRA does not implement alternative approaches. When a user's scenario does not fit standard categories, MIRA flags that FCR 26 (alternative approach with RFCB approval) is the path forward.
